title: Lemony Fennel Salmon
author: Kenzi
ingredients:
1 lbs - 1.3 lbs salmon
1 large lemon, sliced
Fennel, leaves and bulb separated
Dill
instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 400F.
2. Dice fennel bulb. It can be baked along with the salmon.
3. Assemble salmon strips, fennel, dill, lemon slices in a baking dish. Sprinkle olive oil, season generously with salt and pepper.
4. Bake for 25-30 mins.
notes: Can be paired with root vegetables such as potatoes or carrots; and salads.

title: Shrimp Etouffeé
author: Cheryl Dobos
ingredients:
1 stick butter
½ cup diced red pepper
½ cup diced celery
½ cup diced onion
1 (14.5oz) can diced tomatoes with green chilis
Chopped green onions, for garnish
Cooked rice
1 lb shrimp
1 tsp thyme
2 bay leaves
Cajun seasoning mix, to taste:
1 tbsp salt
1 tbsp dried oregano
1 tbsp paprika
1 tbsp cayenne pepper
1 tbsp ground black pepper
1 (14.5oz) can cream of celery soup
instructions:
1. Melt butter in a large frying pan with medium heat. Add pepper, celery, onion and sauté. Add diced tomatoes, let the mixture simmer for 15 minutes.
2. Add in shrimp, thyme, bay leaves, cajun seasoning mix, and cook for 3-5 minutes. Be careful not to overcook the shrimp.
3. Fold in the cream of celery and cook until warmed through.
4. Serve with rice and chopped green onions!

title: Spicy Fish and Couscous
author: Tasting Rome
ingredients:
1 lbs amberjack steaks or sea bass fillets, about 1-1/2 inches thick
Sea salt
¼ cup olive oil
2 small yellow onions, diced
1 tbsp hot paprika
1 tbsp peperoncino or red pepper flakes
1 tsp ground caraway seeds
1 tbsp ground cumin
¼ cup tomato paste
1-1/2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
3 cups hot, cooked couscous
instructions:
1. Salt fish on all sides and let stand at room temperature for about 20 minutes while you make the sauce.
2. Heat oil in a medium saucepan over medium-low heat. When it begins to shimmer, add onions, sprinkle with salt and cook, stirring until translucent and very soft, about 20 minutes.
3. Add paprika, peperoncino, caraway and cumin and continue cooking until fragrant, about one minute. Add tomato paste and cook until it turns a deep, brick red, about two minutes.
4. Add lemon juice and one cup (250 mL) water, stirring to blend in. Simmer over low heat, covered, for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
5. Carefully lower fish into the hot sauce and cook over medium heat until it is opaque and cooked through, about 15 minutes, or 10 minutes per inch thickness.
6. Serve with hot, cooked couscous.

title: Tuna Capers Pasta
author: Melissa Clark
ingredients:
Thin pasta, such as spaghetti or linguine
3 tbsp olive oil
3 garlic cloves, thinly sliced
3 scallions, thinly sliced, whites and greens separated
6-10 anchovies, chopped
3 tbsp capers, drained
1 cup torn fresh herbs, such as parsley or dill
1 can (5-6 oz) tuna, drained
Red pepper flakes, for serving
Lemon wedges, for serving
instructions:
1. In a well-salted pot of boiling water, cook pasta until al dente. Drain, saving 1 cup pasta water.
2. In a large skillet, heat the oil over medium. Add garlic and scallion whites, and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute. Add anchovies and capers and cook until anchovies melt and capers and garlic turn golden, 2 to 3 minutes longer. Add 1/2 cup pasta water, let it reduce until there is just a little left in the pan, then add pasta and herbs and toss well to coat. Add tuna and toss well.
3. Serve with red-pepper flakes on top, more herbs, scallion greens, and a drizzle of olive oil. Serve with lemon wedges on the side for squeezing.

title: Pasta with Artichoke Sauce
author: Feasting at Home
ingredients:
8 oz dry pasta (fettucini, linguine, spaghetti)
20 oz sliced mushrooms
2 tsp olive oil
Salt & pepper to taste
Artichoke Sauce:
1 jar artichoke hearts (10-12 oz)
½ cup water
¼ cup olive oil
10 fresh sage leaves
2 garlic cloves
½ tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper
instructions:
1. Bring a big pot of salted water to a boil, cook the pasta to al dente.
2. While the pasta is cooking, in a large skillet, saute the mushrooms over medium heat in a little olive oil. Season with salt and pepper, set aside.
3. Make the artichoke sauce: Drain the artichoke hearts and place them in a blender. (Don't use a food processor, it will not get this sauce creamy enough!) Add the water, olive oil, sage, garlic, salt and pepper. Blend until very smooth.
4. Add the cooked, drained pasta (do not rinse) to the cooked mushrooms in the saute pan. Toss with artichoke sauce and heat up, gently stirring. Taste for salt, add more if necessary.
5. Serve with a side salad as the dish is not quite veggie heavy!

title: Lemony Asparagus Risotto
author: Feasting at Home
ingredients:
1 bunch asparagus
1 large leek (or white onion, diced)
4 tbsp olive oil, divided
6 garlic cloves, rough chopped
1 cup arborio rice
¼ cup white wine
4 cups veggie broth, divided
½ cup basil leaves
1 lemon, zest and some juice
Salt and pepper
Garnish: basil ribbons, pecorino cheese, toasted pine nuts
Optional: serve with Maitake Mushrooms
instructions:
1. Prep asparagus: trim the ends. Cut the tips and set aside, then cut the middles into 1-inch pieces. Reserve 1 ½ cups middles for the asparagus sauce. The rest (tips and middles) will go directly into the risotto at the end.
2. Blanch the asparagus middles in boiling water for about 5 minutes. Reserve 1 cup cooking liquid and drain the rest. Blend the blanched asparagus with 1 cup cooking liquid, 2 tablespoon olive oil and basil leaves until silky smooth, using either a blender or immersion blender. Set this aside to add to risotto at the end.
3. Start risotto: Thinly slice leeks into half moons, rinsing away any dirt, strain. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a pot or dutch oven over medium heat. Add leeks and saute until softened, 5-6 minutes. Add garlic, cook 2 minutes until fragrant.
4. Add arborio rice and stir to coat, 1 minute. Deglaze with white wine and cook the wine off. Add 1 cup hot veggie broth, scraping up any browned bits, and bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat. Let the rice absorb all the broth. Continue adding the hot broth 1 cup at a time, letting the rice absorb it slowly. At the time that you add the last cup of broth, add the pile of asparagus with the tips, letting them cook in the risotto for 3 minutes or so. At this point, rice should be creamy yet slightly al dente.
5. Combine: Stir in asparagus sauce, add salt and pepper, a squeeze of lemon juice and taste. Heat gently over low heat letting it thicken a bit if you like, but take care not to cook too long here. Top with pecorino cheese, basil ribbons, pine nuts, and/or serve with roasted fish, shrimp, grilled chicken or mushrooms.
notes: To serve with Maitake Mushrooms, pan-sear them separately. To clean Maitake mushrooms, brush off any dirt from the root end, and do not get wet. Pan sear in a skillet, in olive oil seasoned with salt and pepper, over medium heat. Cook until the inner leaves are tender and the edges are a little crispy.

title: Butternut Risotto with Leeks
author: Feasting at Home
ingredients:
2 tbsp olive oil
2 cups sliced leeks
4 garlic cloves, rough chopped
8 sage leaves, chopped
1 cup arborio rice
2 heaping cups butternut squash, cubed
¼ cup white wine
4-5 cups vegetable broth
½ tsp nutmeg
2-3 handfuls baby spinach or chopped kale
Optional: parmesan, pecorino, manchego, goat cheese, leek oil, maple glazed pecans
instructions:
1. ROAST BUTTERNUT: Toss the butternut with olive oil, salt and pepper and ROAST the butternut in a 400F oven on a parchment-lined sheet pan until caramelized and tender, 25-30 minutes. At the same time make risotto.
2. RISOTTO: In a large heavy-bottomed pot or dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat and add the washed leeks. Saute until fragrant and tender, covering with the lid for a few minutes to let them steam a bit. Add garlic and sage, saute 2 more minutes until fragrant.
3. Add the rice and saute 1 minute, stirring. Add a splash of white wine, and cook this off. Add the salt, pepper and nutmeg. Add 1-2 cups warm stock (enough to cover the rice), stir and bring to a gentle simmer. Simmer until most of the liquid is absorbed. Continue adding broth 1 cup at a time, letting the rice absorb it slowly, stirring often over medium-low heat, until the rice is plumped, slightly al dente, yet creamy, about 20-25 minutes. If adding kale, add it with the last cup of broth. If adding spinach, you can stir it in at the end. Keep the risotto thick and hearty or add more stock to loosen it up a bit.
4. Stir in the roasted butternut and spinach and optional cheese or butter. Taste, season and adjust salt and pepper.
5. Garnish with the leek oil and maple glazed pecans.

title: Spicy Pasta E Fagioli
author: Nana's soup cookbook
ingredients:
¼ cup olive oil
2 cloves garlic, minced
1-1 ½ tsp ground pepper
¼ tsp crushed red pepper flakes
½ cup finely chopped onion
1 2oz can anchovies, drained and chopped
2 15oz cans white beans, with their liquid
1 cup dry small pasta (ditalini)
3 cups low-sodium vegetable broth
1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
½ cup freshly grated parmesan
Kosher salt
instructions:
1. In a large pot, heat the olive oil over medium-high heat. Add the garlic, black pepper, red pepper flakes and saute for 30 seconds. Add the onion and anchovies and saute until the onion is soft and translucent, about 2 minutes.
2. Add the beans with their liquid, the ditalini, and the broth. Let the mixture come to a boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer. Let simmer for 10 minutes.
3. Just before serving, stir in the lemon juice and parmesan.

title: Green Pea Soup
author: Vincent
ingredients:
150g green peas
1 small head broccoli
Chicken stock
Milk
1 large potato, cubed
Half white onion, diced
Salt, pepper, butter
instructions:
1. Bring a large pot of water to boil, blanch broccoli for 1-2 mins. This is to preserve the green color.
2. Prep onion and potato.
3. Saute onion on medium-low heat, add potato and a small chunk of butter, stir a bit.
4. Then add blanched broccoli and peas. Add chicken stock, just enough to almost cover all the veggies.
5. Blend soup with an immersion blender. Season with salt and pepper. Serve with baguette.

title: Coconut Corn Chowder
author: Feasting at Home
ingredients:
1-2 tbsp olive oil
2 large leeks, thinly sliced into rings
2 cups celery, diced
4 garlic cloves, rough chopped
3 cups corn (frozen is fine)
3 cups diced baby potatoes, thinly sliced into ¼ inch thick rounds
3 cups vegetable broth
1 tsp salt
½ tsp pepper
2 bay leaves
1 tbsp fresh thyme (1 ½ tsp dried)
14oz can coconut milk
½ tsp apple cider vinegar or lemon juice
½ tsp ground turmeric
Pinch cayenne
instructions:
1. Slice leeks and soak in a bowl of water, separate rings, rinse and drain to remove all sediment. (Leeks from Trader Joe's usually contain less dirt.)
2. In a heavy-bottomed pot or dutch oven, heat oil over medium-high heat. Add leeks, saute 3 minutes stirring until just begin to get tender, lower heat to medium. Cover for 3-4 minutes and let them get more tender. Add celery and garlic and lower heat to medium-low and saute until leeks are meltingly tender, about 5-6 minutes.
3. Add corn, potatoes, veggie broth, salt, pepper, bay leaves, thyme and bring to a simmer. Cover, turn heat to medium-low and let simmer until potatoes are tender, 8-10 minutes.
4. Remove 4 cups of veggies from the soup and set aside. Add coconut milk to the pot and blend the remaining soup in the pot using an immersion blender. (Alternatively, blend half of the soup in a blender.) Pour the veggies back into the pot.
5. Taste and season with salt and pepper if needed. Add the vinegar and pinch of cayenne if you want a hint of brightness or kick. Whisk in a little ground turmeric to give it a golden happy color.

title: Kale and Vegetable Soup
author: Nana's soup cookbook
ingredients:
2 tbsp olive oil
3 medium carrots, cut into medium dice
1 large yellow onion, cut into medium dice
2 medium cloves garlic, minced
2 cups ½-inch cubed peeled butternut squash (about 1 pound squash)
¼ tsp ground allspice
Pinch of cayenne pepper; more to taste
Kosher salt
1 quart low-sodium vegetable stock, plus 2-3 more cups for reheating
1 14.5 oz can no-salt-added diced tomatoes
4 sprigs fresh thyme
2 cups lightly packed, coarsely chopped kale
1 can lower-salt canned chickpeas
instructions:
1. Heat the oil in a large soup pot over medium-high heat. Add the carrots and onions and cook, stirring occasionally, until they begin to soften, about 6 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute more. Add the squash, allspice, cayenne, and 1 tsp salt and stir to combine. Add the broth, tomatoes with their juice, and thyme. Bring to a boil, reduce the heat to medium, cover, and simmer for 10 minutes.
2. Add the kale and the chickpeas and cook uncovered until the squash is tender and kale is wilted, about another 10 minutes. Discard the thyme sprigs before serving. Add more salt, pepper, and cayenne to taste.

title: Beet Poke
author: Feasting at Home
ingredients:
3 cups beets, cut into ½ inch cubes
½ tsp sea salt
1 cup water
2-3 scallions, chopped
¼ cup cilantro, chopped
2 tbsp sesame seeds
Shredded nori (optional)
Soba noodles
Extras: Snow peas, Avocado, Quick pickled radishes (see Gochujang Chicken)
Poke Marinade (for 2):
1 tbsp soy sauce
1 ½ tbsp sesame oil
1 tbsp rice vinegar
1 ½ tsp grated ginger
2 tsp lime
2-3 tsp maple syrup or honey
¼ tsp chili flakes (optional)
instructions:
1. Trim both sides off of the beets, skin them, and cube them. Place beet cubes in a saucepan with the cold water and salt. Bring to a boil and simmer on low heat for 20 minutes or until easily forked. Remove beets from heat and drain off any remaining water, place beets in a bowl.
2. While beets are simmering, make the quick pickled radish (could be made ahead), poke marinade, and lastly soba.
3. When it's ready to serve, assemble the ingredients in bowls: soba, beets, snow peas, radishes, avocado, and seaweed. Drizzle marinade over soba and vegetables, and sprinkle scallions, cilantro, and sesame seeds.

title: Chana Masala
author: Feasting at Home
ingredients:
4-5 cups cooked or canned chickpeas
3 tbsp ghee or coconut oil
2 bay leaves
2 tsp cumin seeds (whole)
1 tsp fennel seeds
2 onions, diced
4 fat garlic cloves, rough chopped
½-1 jalapeno or 1 serrano chili, finely diced
1 tbsp fresh ginger, minced
1 tsp garam masala
1 tsp ground cumin
1 tsp ground coriander
½ tsp chili powder or paprika
½ tsp ground turmeric
2 medium tomatoes, diced (and their juices) or 14-ounce can tomato puree
1 teaspoon salt
¼-½ cup water
Optional: 1 tsp honey or sugar
Serve with: rice or naan, pickled onions
instructions:
1. In a large pot or dutch oven, over medium-high heat, heat ghee and add whole bay leaves and cumin seeds and fennel seeds stirring 1-2 minutes until fragrant and golden. Add onions. Saute 5-7 minutes until golden, lowering the heat to medium. You really want these to deeply caramelize so they add a nice sweetness. Add garlic, ginger and diced chili, saute 2-3 minutes.
2. Add all the spices — garam masala, ground cumin, coriander, chili powder, turmeric.
3. Give a stir then add the tomatoes and their juices, stirring constantly, for about 3 minutes, scraping up any browned bits. Once the tomatoes start to break down, add 1/4-1/2 cup water, salt, and chickpeas. Let simmer on low for 10-15 minutes. Taste and adjust salt. If it tastes bitter, add a little sugar or honey to balance.
4. Serve with rice or naan, and pickled onions.

title: Moroccan Mujadara
author: Feasting at Home
ingredients:
1 cup green lentils
1 cup uncooked white rice
1 ½ tbsp olive oil
2-3 fat shallots, thinly sliced
4 cloves garlic, roughly chopped
4 cups water
Cherry tomatoes, halved
½ red cabbage, thinly chopped
Handful of pine nuts
2 tsp cumin
1 tsp coriander
1 tsp allspice
½ tsp cinnamon
½ tsp turmeric
¼ tsp ground ginger
1 ½ tsp kosher salt
instructions:
1. Rinse lentils and rice.
2. In a large dutch oven, heat oil and cook the shallots, stirring often until golden and caramelized. Remove half and save them for garnish at the end.
3. Add garlic to the remaining shallots and stir for 1 minute. Add rinsed lentils and rice, all the spices, and water to the pot. Give a good stir. Bring the mixture to a simmer and let it simmer with lid on for 20 minutes, stirring once or twice half way through. Add water if necessary.
4. While the rice and lentils are cooking, chop red cabbage. Sauté with some olive oil, salt and pepper, approximately 10 minutes.
5. To serve, dish lentils and rice into bowl, garnish with caramelized shallots, sautéed red cabbage, cherry tomatoes, and pine nuts.

title: Thai Basil Pork
author: Kenzi
ingredients:
1 lbs ground pork
Half bag of TJ green beans, chopped into smaller bits
50g Thai basil
2 large garlic cloves
1 fried egg for each serving
Red pepper flakes
Sauce:
25g fish sauce
25g soy sauce
15g oyster sauce
10g Shaoxing wine
1 tsp cane sugar
instructions:
1. Make the sauce.
2. Cook green beans until tender, dish aside.
3. Cook ground pork, add garlic and sauce when it's almost cooked; add green beans and basil.
4. Fry eggs in the meantime.

title: Bean Sprout Side Dish
author: Maangchi
ingredients:
1 lbs bean sprouts, rinsed and drained
1 tsp kosher salt
2 garlic cloves, minced
1 green onion, chopped
½ tsp hot pepper flakes
1 tsp oyster sauce
1 tsp roasted sesame seeds
2 tsp sesame oil
instructions:
1. Bring a pot of water to a boil. Toss in bean sprouts and salt, boil over medium heat for 3-4 minutes.
2. Put the cooked soybean sprouts in a mixing bowl. Add garlic, hot pepper flakes, green onion, oyster sauce, sesame seeds, and toasted sesame oil and mix by hand.
3. Serve as a side dish to rice.

title: Pickled Red Onions
author: Feasting at Home
ingredients:
½ red onion, very thinly sliced
½ cup white vinegar, or apple cider vinegar
½ cup water
¾ tsp kosher salt
1 ½-2 tbsp sugar
1-2 tsp whole spices (see below)
For a Mexican version: use whole cumin and coriander seeds and oregano added to the liquid
For a Nordic version: add fresh dill, caraway and peppercorns
instructions:
1. Thinly slice the red onion. Place onion along with vinegar, water, salt, sugar, and whole spices in a small pot. Bring to a simmer, simmer for 1 minute, stirring.
2. Remove from the stove and let cool.
notes: It takes a while to bring the mix to a simmer, and onion will continue to pickle as it cools. This will last 2-3 weeks in the fridge. Yields 1 ½ cups.

title: Roasted Portobello Mushroom with Walnut Coffee Sauce
author: Feasting at Home
ingredients:
4 extra large portobello mushroom
2 tbsp olive oil
1 tbsp balsamic vinegar
Pinch of salt
Walnut Coffee Sauce:
1 ½ tbsp olive oil
1 extra large shallot, roughly diced (about ½ cup)
2 garlic cloves, roughly chopped
½ cup walnuts
¾ cup coffee (cold or decaf is ok)
¼ tsp salt
¼ tsp pepper
½ tsp miso
½ tsp balsamic
instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 400F.
2. Mix oil and vinegar in a small bowl and brush the portobello mushroom on both sides. Sprinkle with salt and pepper and place gills side down, on a parchment lined sheet pan. Bake for 20-25 minutes until tender.
3. Make the sauce while the mushrooms are roasting. Heat oil in a small non-stick pan over medium heat. Saute shallot and garlic until fragrant and tender, about 4-5 minutes. Add walnuts and stir for 2 minutes. Pour the mixture and coffee into a blender, add salt, pepper, miso paste, balsamic, and blend until silky smooth.
4. When the portobello mushrooms are done, either slice them or serve them whole. Serve with cauliflower mash, mashed potatoes, quinoa, or wild rice!

title: Cranberry Shortbread Cookies
author: Mom
ingredients:
230g all-purpose flour
65g sugar
1 egg
65g dried cranberries, chopped into smaller bits
120g unsalted butter (1 stick), at room temperature
instructions:
1. Cream butter and sugar, then add the egg. Add flour and dried cranberries, mix with your hands. Knead a little until the dough comes together. The dough should be quite soft.
2. Place dough on a piece of cling wrap. Shape the dough into a rectangular log. Seal cling wrap and freeze dough for 1 hour in freezer.
3. Preheat oven to 340F when you're ready to bake. Cut the frozen dough with a sharp knife, into 13-14 thin rectangular pieces. Bake for 20 minutes or until slightly golden. (Always check at 15 minutes just to make sure, but always add another 5 minutes at the end.)
4. Let cool and enjoy!

title: Blueberry Crumble
author: Inspired Taste
ingredients:
For the filling:
24 oz fresh blueberries
2 tbsp sugar
2 tbsp flour
1 tbsp lemon juice, or water (optional)
For the Crumble Topping:
¾ cup (100g) flour
¾ cup (65g) old-fashioned oats
½ cup (100g) sugar
½ cup (115g) unsalted butter, melted; or substitute ½ cup coconut oil
⅛ tsp fine sea salt
instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 375 degrees Fahrenheit.
2. Make filling: Add blueberries, lemon juice, 2 tablespoons of flour, sugar, and pinch of salt to a 9-inch pie dish (or use a 2-quart baking dish). Toss well until combined.
3. Make Crumble Topping: Combine flour, oats, sugar, and the salt in a medium bowl. Add the melted butter then stir until all the flour has been moistened by the butter and topping is crumbly. Sprinkle over blueberry filling. (Use your hands to do this; as you sprinkle, press the crumbles together to create larger clumps of topping.)
4. Bake 25 to 35 minutes until juices are thickened and the topping has turned light golden brown. Cool 10 minutes, and then serve.

title: French Apple Cake
author: Once Upon a Chef
ingredients:
1 cup all-purpose flour
1 tsp baking powder
¼ tsp salt
1 stick (½ cup) unsalted butter, at room temperature
⅔ cup granulated sugar
2 large eggs
1 tsp vanilla extract
3 tbsp dark rum
2 baking apples, peeled, cored and cut into ½-inch cubes (honeycrisp, fuji, or Granny Smith)
instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 350°F and set an oven rack in the middle position. Grease a 9-inch springform or regular cake pan with butter or nonstick cooking spray. If using a regular cake pan, line the bottom of the pan with parchment paper and grease again.
2. In a small bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder and salt.
3. Using a handheld mixer with beaters or a stand mixer with the paddle attachment, cream the butter and granulated sugar until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes. Add the eggs, one at a time, beating well and scraping down the sides of the bowl after each addition. Beat in the vanilla and rum. Don't worry if the batter looks grainy at this point; that's okay. Add the flour mixture and mix on low speed until just combined. Using a rubber spatula, fold in the chopped apples.
4. Scrape the batter into the prepared pan and even the top. Sprinkle evenly with 1 tablespoon of granulated sugar. Bake for about 40 minutes, or until the cake is golden and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. Allow the cake to cool on a rack in the pan. Once cool, run a blunt knife around the edges of the cake. If using a springform pan, remove the sides. If using a regular cake pan, carefully invert the cake onto the rack, remove the parchment paper, then gently flip the cake over and place right-side-up on a platter. Cake can be served warm or room temperature, plain or with lightly sweetened whipped cream or vanilla ice cream.

title: Classic Oatmeal Raisin Cookies
author: Melissa Clark
ingredients:
½ cup/113g unsalted butter, softened
½ cup/90g dark brown sugar
⅙ cup/30g granulated sugar
1 egg
½ tsp/7.5ml vanilla extract
¾ cup/93g all purpose flour
Little less than ½ tsp salt
½ tsp baking soda
½ tsp ground cinnamon
1 ½ cups/135g rolled oats
¾ cup/112g raisins
instructions:
1. Heat oven to 350 degrees. Butter two large cookie sheets, or line them with parchment paper or reusable silicone liners.
2. Using an electric mixer, beat butter in a large bowl until creamy. Add brown and granulated sugars, then beat until fluffy, about 2 minutes. Beat in egg until fully incorporated. Then, beat in vanilla extract.
3. In a separate bowl, use a wooden spoon or spatula to mix together the flour, salt, baking soda, and cinnamon. Set mixer on low speed, and beat flour mixture into the butter mixture. Stir in oats and raisins.
4. Spoon out dough by large tablespoonfuls onto prepared cookie sheets, leaving at least 2 inches between each cookie.
5. Bake until cookie edges turn golden brown, about 9 to 13 minutes. Centers will still be quite soft, but they will firm up as the cookies cool. Cool completely on a wire rack. Store in an airtight container at room temperature.
